metadata.title: Staatsbürgerinnen und Staatsbürger von morgen: Zur Wirksamkeit politischer Bildung in der Schweiz. Ein Vergleich mit 37 anderen Ländern

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses ICCS 2009 sampling with a multi-stage stratified design: stratification by school type and language region, PPS selection of schools, and random selection of classes within schools. It reports participation thresholds for inclusion of countries (at least 85% at school and student levels, or 75% combined) and describes exclusions of schools with only students with intellectual disabilities and very small schools (<6 students in the target grade). The manuscript does not report the specific student weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT) nor any replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation in the analysis cannot be verified from the provided text. For ICCS analyses, analysts should apply the complex survey weights supplied with the ICCS international database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the clustered design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report focuses on descriptive and comparative results from ICCS scales (e.g., political knowledge and understanding on an international scale, and attitudinal/behavioral scales) rather than training predictive ML models on PV-based cognitive achievement outcomes. Plausible Values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of PV-combining rules for an ML prediction pipeline. Missing-data handling is not documented in the provided text; however, the study’s reported outputs are primarily scale-based summaries and subgroup comparisons, and the manuscript does not specify an imputation/deletion strategy for missing questionnaire/test responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The target population is students in Grade 8; if the average age in a country is below 13.5 years, Grade 9 students are used instead. The sampling is multi-stage and stratified: schools are stratified by school type and language region, then selected with PPS (Probability Proportional to Size), excluding schools attended exclusively by students with intellectual disabilities and excluding very small schools (<6 students in the target grade). Within selected schools, classes are randomly selected (typically one class per school). Countries are included in analyses only if participation meets thresholds on both school and student levels (at least 85% on each level, or 75% combined). In Switzerland, the report states 2,924 students participated.

data.outcome_summary: This ICCS 2009 first-results report compares civic and citizenship education outcomes across 38 participating countries, focusing on students aged 14–15 (Grade 8, or Grade 9 where needed to meet the age criterion). The study uses a 45-minute cognitive test on political knowledge and understanding (80 tasks across seven booklets) and a 40-minute student questionnaire capturing attitudes, beliefs, interests, and engagement; an additional European module is administered to participating European students. Political knowledge is scaled to an international metric with mean 500 and SD 100, and three performance levels are defined by score thresholds. The report provides cross-country comparisons for multiple civic outcomes (knowledge, trust in institutions, national attitudes, rights attitudes toward women and migrants, interest and discussion participation, political self-efficacy, and engagement intentions/behaviors), with Switzerland generally above the international mean on knowledge but below-average on several engagement and self-efficacy indicators. Methodologically, the manuscript describes the complex sampling design and inclusion thresholds but does not document PV-combining rules or missing-data handling in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an ICCS first-results comparative report rather than an empirical machine-learning prediction study. The provided text contains no ML model training/evaluation, no PV-combining strategy, and no explicit missing-data handling procedure; therefore, ML-specific fields (algorithms, predictive targets) are intentionally left empty. The extraction is sparse for per-country student counts and for weighting variable names because the report summarizes sampling and participation rates at a high level rather than providing full analytic-sample breakdowns and weight implementation details.
